snippets.text: Intertrigo is a superficial inflammatory skin condition that affects flexural surfaces, such as the axillae, abdominal folds, and perineum. This condition is often triggered or aggravated by warm temperatures, friction, moisture, maceration, and poor ventilation. The Latin origins of the term "intertrigo"—inter (meaning "between") and terere (meaning "to rub")—illustrate the condition's physiology. Intertrigo often becomes secondarily infected, particularly by Candida, although other viral or bacterial pathogens may also contribute to its pathogenesis.
snippets.title: Intertrigo: causes, prevention and management. > Continuing Education Activity

snippets.text: Intertrigo can occur at any age and is primarily diagnosed clinically; in more complex cases, further evaluation, such as culturing or skin scraping, may be needed to identify specific pathogens. Intertrigo typically presents as erythematous patches of varying intensity, which may progress to erosions and secondary lesions due to irritation or manipulation.[3]
snippets.title: Intertrigo: causes, prevention and management. > Introduction

snippets.text: The differential diagnosis for intertrigo is extensive, as many other conditions can occur in the flexural surfaces. However, it is crucial to rule out infections and identify the specific infectious agent to provide the appropriate antimicrobial therapy needed to eliminate the offending organism. Bacteria, viruses, dermatophytes, and Candida species can all cause intertrigo or provoke a secondary infection.[16] Once an infection has been ruled out, further investigation of other similarly presenting conditions commonly found in the flexural areas can proceed.
